The Associated Press reported her statement and described contacts with Russian President Vladimir Putin concerning separated children. According to that account, Melania Trump had written to Putin in August, and Donald Trump delivered the letter during their meeting in Alaska. She said Putin responded and that an open channel of communication followed. Her announcement described the reunifications as the result of ongoing discussions, but the report is evidence of what she publicly stated, not independent verification of the circumstances of every child’s return. The children’s individual identities, precise dates of return, and the specific involvement of each official were not established by the reviewed material. This entry therefore records a documented public announcement rather than making an unqualified assertion that every reported reunion or diplomatic claim has been independently audited. Broader assertions about personal credit or guarantees of future reunions are excluded.

proposal.title: Trump Names Michael Ellis Deputy CIA Director; Ellis Sworn In February 10
proposal.description_short: Trump appointed Michael Ellis CIA deputy director in February 2025; the agency confirms Ellis was sworn in on February 10.
proposal.description_medium: The Washington Post reported on February 3, 2025, that President Donald Trump selected Michael Ellis as deputy director of the Central Intelligence Agency. A CIA release confirms Ellis was sworn in on February 10. The agency lists earlier national-security roles at the NSA, National Security Council, House Intelligence Committee, and Navy Reserve. This entry concerns the documented appointment and assumption of office, not claims of political loyalty or unrelated intelligence-personnel decisions.
proposal.description_long: On February 3, 2025, the Washington Post reported that President Donald Trump had named lawyer Michael Ellis deputy director of the Central Intelligence Agency. Ellis was to serve under CIA Director John Ratcliffe, and the newspaper noted that the deputy position did not require Senate confirmation. A separate CIA announcement establishes that Ellis was sworn in on February 10. The agency identified his prior service as general counsel of the National Security Agency, senior director for intelligence programs at the National Security Council, general counsel of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and a Navy Reserve intelligence officer. CIA Director Ratcliffe welcomed Ellis in the agency announcement. These sources independently support the reported appointment and the later swearing-in, which are kept as two dates rather than presented as a single February 3 oath. The sources do not, by themselves, demonstrate the motives for Trump’s selection or the effects of Ellis’s tenure. Other claimed intelligence-agency dismissals, security-clearance decisions, and reorganizations were separate matters and are not imported into this entry.
proposal.factual_scope: Selection February 3; oath February 10; no inferred motives.
